In mathematics, '''algebraic homotopy''' is a research program on [[homotopy theory]] proposed by [[J.H.C. Whitehead]] in his 1950 ICM talk, where he described it as:<ref>Baues, Homotopy Types in Chapter 1 in Handbook of Algebraic Topology</ref><ref>NB: we need a citation to the original source.</ref>

{{quote|The ultimate object of algebraic homotopy is to construct a purely algebraic theory, which is equivalent to homotopy theory in the same sort of way that 'analytic' is equivalent to 'pure' projective geometry.}}

In spirit, the program is somehow similar to Grothendieck's [[homotopy hypothesis]]. However, according to Ronnie Brown, "Looking again at Esquisses d'un Progamme, it seems that programme has currently little relation to Whitehead's."<ref>https://mathoverflow.net/questions/266738/current-status-of-grothendiecks-homotopy-hypothesis-and-whiteheads-algebraic-h</ref>
